subject: Payeta - reserved capacity sizing: session & token profile questionnaire
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@payeta.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payeta - reserved capacity sizing: session & token profile questionnaire

Hi Lina,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday — excited to work through sizing for Payeta's reserved capacity pilot. To get engineering aligned, can you fill in the quick profile below (or attach a sampled export) so we can map to GPU SKUs and expected concurrency? A few specifics that help the most: 

- Traffic shape: typical sustained requests per second (avg) and observed peak QPS/day.
- Session semantics: are you pinning sessions (long-lived KV cache) or stateless requests? Typical session length in minutes and % of requests re-using a session.
- Prompt/response token distributions: median and 95th for both prompt and model response.
- Percent of requests that require streaming vs full-response batch.
- Target P99 latency SLO for interactive endpoints and acceptable cost trade-offs (e.g., prefer higher latency tolerance to reduce unit cost).
- OAuth / signed requests per minute and whether you plan to use inference-level key sharding.

If you have a CSV export of sampled traffic (timestamp, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id, is_streamed) attach it and we can run a small estimator. I attached a lightweight template you can drop values into.

Quick ask: can we get the filled profile or sample export by EOD Thursday so we can route to capacity planning for a June pilot?

Thanks —
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: workload_profile_template.csv (stub)

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@payeta.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payeta - reserved capacity sizing: session & token profile questionnaire

Hi Avery —

Thanks, yes we can do that. Attaching a 48-hour sample and a short note on our session model. Highlights:

- Sustained: ~55 RPS across our EU+US frontend, peak ~320 RPS during batch ingestion windows (midnight PST).
- Session model: we maintain session affinity for chatbot flows (avg session length 18 minutes); ~38% of requests reuse KV state within the session window. Most other endpoints are stateless (webhooks, summarization).
- Tokens (sample percentiles): prompt median 120 tokens / p95 920 tokens; response median 48 tokens / p95 640 tokens.
- Streaming: ~12% are streaming responses (real-time transcription+chat).
- Latency: interactive endpoints target P99 <= 350 ms. For background batch jobs, we accept up to 3s.
- Auth: we use a rotating API key model from our gateway; expect ~8k signed requests/minute at peak.

I've attached payeta_workload_sample.csv and a network diagram (architecture_v1.png). Let me know if you want a longer window or additional fields.

Best,
Lina Torres
Head of Platform Integrations, Payeta
lina.torres@payeta.com

Attachments: payeta_workload_sample.csv, architecture_v1.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@payeta.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payeta - reserved capacity sizing: session & token profile questionnaire

Thanks Lina — this is great context. A couple quick clarifying questions from infra sizing perspective so we pick the right GPU mix and tenancy model: 

1) Session KV cache size: what is the average and 95th percentile KV size per session (MB)? This determines memory footprint when we co-locate multiple sessions on a GPU.
2) For the 320 RPS peak, is that concentrated into a 10–15 minute window (burst) or sustained over several hours? Also, is the peak primarily read-only inference or does it include heavy embedding/long-form summarization jobs?
3) Token ceiling: are there many long-run streaming responses that exceed 2k tokens (we saw p95 response 640 but curious about tails).
4) Any compliance constraints for model variants (e.g., forced on-prem for certain customers in your platform)?

If you can drop answers inline or in the CSV, we'll run an occupancy estimate and share a recommended SKU mix (A100/RTX equivalent, quantized vs fp16, and concurrency per instance).

Quick note: if you'd rather we run a short load simulator against a staging key, we can coordinate a 2-hour window next week and produce latency-concurrency curves.

—Karthik
Senior Pre-Sales Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@payeta.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payeta - reserved capacity sizing: session & token profile questionnaire

Hi Karthik / Avery —

Answers below and I've appended a second CSV with KV-size samples: 

1) KV size per session: median 0.9 MB, p95 6.2 MB (we keep conversational context + few embeddings cached).
2) Peak shape: the 320 RPS is a ~12-minute burst tied to our daily content ingestion; outside that it's usually under 80 RPS sustained. The peak mixes both short chat reads and heavier summarization — roughly 65/35 read-to-heavy.
3) Token ceiling: rare tails exceed 2k tokens (~0.4% of requests). p99 response around 1.9k.
4) Compliance: a subset of customers (gov/health) require a private deployment; for the pilot we are fine with Redwood Dedicated in our VPC.

We can also schedule the 2-hour staging run next Tuesday morning (US-West) — we can provide a staging key and a replay of a 90-minute slice.

Lina

Attachment: payeta_workload_sample_kv.csv

--
Lina Torres
Head of Platform Integrations, Payeta
